requirements.requirement: usb-storage module cannot be loaded immediately (now) on node1
requirements.summary: Blacklist config with 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' was created; modprobe (normal and forced) failed with 'Invalid argument' immediately after, and lsmod confirmed the module was not loaded.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage module load is prevented after a reboot (persistent across boot)
requirements.summary: initramfs was rebuilt via update-initramfs -u -k all and confirmed to contain the blacklist config file. A real reboot was then performed (boot_id changed from 28ae5f98... to b931f7ed...), and post-reboot checks show usb_storage still unloaded, modprobe still fails with the same install-override error, and the config file is intact — directly demonstrating persistence through an actual reboot rather than just static configuration.

overall_summary: The executor blacklisted usb-storage via /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with a hard install-override, rebuilt the initramfs, and directly proved both immediate and post-reboot enforcement: pre-reboot modprobe failures, an actual reboot evidenced by a changed boot_id, and identical modprobe failures plus an intact config and unloaded module after the node came back up. This fully satisfies both the 'now' and 'after reboot' requirements with a genuine before/disruption/after transition rather than configuration alone.
limitations: No physical or virtual USB storage device was present/attached to actually attempt a real hot-plug and observe non-attachment; verification relies on modprobe/lsmod behavior rather than an actual device-insertion test, which is a reasonable and standard substitute for this kind of task.

The lsinitramfs -x extraction to /tmp/initrd-check was not explicitly cleaned up by the executor; its absence in the post-executor snapshot is inferred from the reboot clearing tmpfs rather than from an explicit cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were narrowly scoped to the task: one config file created, one initramfs rebuild, verification commands, and the mandatory reboot cycle. One minor unnecessary mutation: in cmd-4df70d7e507d49c8 the executor ran mkdir -p /tmp/initrd-check and extracted the entire initramfs into it via lsinitramfs -x, even though the preceding grep against the initramfs listing already confirmed the blacklist file's presence — this extraction was redundant diagnostic overkill rather than a needed verification step. It was bounded and low-risk, and self-cleaned as a side effect of the subsequent reboot (tmpfs is reset on boot, and the after-executor temporary-files snapshot shows no /tmp/initrd-check residue), so it carries low severity. No failed services, no package-health issues, and no other stray files are present in either the before/after comparisons; the only other executor-caused diffs (boot-identity, listening-socket ephemeral ports, systemd-private temp dirs) are expected byproducts of the reboot itself, not unwanted residue.
